archud.perf.e_item.desc: Render distance of items on the ground.
archud.perf.e_cap.desc: Beyond the limit, entities farther than 16 blocks are skipped.
archud.perf.e_dynamic.desc: Below 45 FPS all distances shrink to 80%, below 30 to 60%.
archud.perf.e_invisible.desc: Skip models of invisible mobs far away.
archud.perf.l_armor.desc: Armor on mobs only up close.
archud.perf.l_head.desc: Worn heads and pumpkins only up close.
archud.perf.l_arrows.desc: Arrows stuck in bodies only up close.
archud.perf.l_other.desc: Extra model layers from mods only up close.
archud.perf.n_tag_dist.desc: Names and tags only up close.
archud.perf.n_mob_tags.desc: Mob name tags are hidden; players stay.
archud.perf.x_item_single.desc: Item stacks on the ground draw one model instead of 2–5.
archud.perf.x_glint.desc: Removes the extra render pass of enchanted items.
archud.perf.b_campfire.desc: Items on campfires only up close.
archud.perf.b_modded.desc: Render distance of modded block entities.
archud.perf.b_walls.desc: Chests, signs etc. behind walls are skipped.
archud.perf.p_limit.desc: No new particles above the limit.
archud.perf.p_smoke.desc: A third of campfire, furnace and torch smoke.
archud.perf.p_crit.desc: A third of crit and enchant particles.
archud.perf.p_dust.desc: A third of redstone dust particles.
archud.perf.w_rain.desc: Rain and snow are not drawn (sound stays).
archud.perf.w_fog.desc: Land fog off (water and lava fog stay).
archud.perf.w_biome_blend.desc: Hard biome color edges (faster chunk builds).
archud.perf.w_chunk_priority.desc: Builds chunks near the player first.
archud.perf.s_menu_fps.desc: Max 30 FPS on title and world screens.
archud.perf.s_bg_fps.desc: Few frames while the window is unfocused.
archud.perf.s_minimized.desc: Minimized game barely uses the system.
archud.perf.s_lazy_anim.desc: Texture animations pause when the world is hidden.
archud.perf.s_gc.desc: Garbage collection when leaving a world.
archud.perf.s_world_behind_menu.desc: Settings and pause show the last world frame.
archud.perf.a_minimap_30fps.desc: Minimap content redraws 30 times a second.
archud.perf.a_map_scan.desc: Half the time spent mapping terrain.
archud.perf.a_hud_anim.desc: No smoothing of HUD bars and blocks.
archud.fx.shader.desc: Light single-pass post effect (~0.3 ms per frame). Turns itself off with Iris/OptiFine shaderpacks.
archud.fx.hdr.desc: Lifted shadows, local contrast and a filmic tone curve — HDR-like on a regular display.
archud.fx.vibrance.desc: Boosts dull colors more than vivid ones.
archud.fx.shaderpack.desc: A shaderpack is on — the built-in shader and render scale are skipped.
archud.fx.render_scale.desc: The world renders at a lower resolution and is upscaled — more FPS on weak GPUs. The UI stays sharp.
archud.fx.upscaler.desc: Bilinear — fastest; FSR-style — bicubic filter and RCAS sharpening; Arc TSR (like DLSS) — frame accumulation, sharpest, but fast-moving mobs may leave slight trails.
archud.fx.resolution.desc: The resolution the world is rendered at.
archud.fx.dlss.desc: Arc TSR temporal upscaler — same idea as DLSS 2 and FSR 2: the world is rendered at a lower resolution with a sub-pixel offset, and frames are accumulated and reprojected using depth and camera motion. Works on any GPU. Real NVIDIA DLSS can't be used in Minecraft Java: it only works through DirectX/Vulkan and the NVIDIA driver, while the game renders with OpenGL. DLAA — no downscaling, anti-aliasing only.
archud.fx.waving_plants.desc: Grass, flowers and saplings sway in the wind.
archud.fx.waving_leaves.desc: Leaves and vines move slightly (leaves render without mipmaps).
archud.fx.waving_sodium.desc: Sodium uses its own chunk shaders — waving plants do not work with it.
archud.perf.enabled.desc: How many optimization switches are on.
archud.perf.preset.max.desc: Everything on: shorter distances, fewer particles and effects.
archud.perf.preset.balanced.desc: Noticeable FPS gain with almost no visual change.
archud.perf.r_adaptive.desc: Keeps the target FPS at any render distance: when FPS drops below the target, far chunks stop being drawn (1 chunk per step, never below a third of the distance); when FPS recovers they come back. Chunks stay loaded, so distance returns instantly. Fog follows the edge. Not active with Sodium/Embeddium (they render chunks themselves).
archud.perf.r_upload_budget.desc: Built chunks are uploaded to the GPU for at most ~3 ms per frame, the rest in later frames. Removes stutter when flying fast with a large render distance. Not active with Sodium/Embeddium.
archud.perf.t_activation.desc: When the server can't keep up (tick over 45 ms), mobs, items and XP farther than this from players update every 4th tick. Mobs in combat, hurt, leashed, bosses, projectiles and vehicles always tick normally.
archud.perf.t_dyn_sim.desc: If the server lags for over 5 seconds, simulation distance is temporarily lowered by 1 (not below 4) until it catches up, then restored.
archud.perf.t_spawn.desc: While the server lags, natural mob spawning runs every other tick.
archud.perf.t_random.desc: Under very heavy lag (tick over 80 ms), random block ticks (plant growth, grass spread) happen half as often.
archud.perf.t_smooth_entities.desc: At low TPS mob positions arrive rarely and they move in jumps. The client stretches smooth movement over the whole interval between updates.
archud.fx.api.desc: Which graphics API the game renders with.
archud.fx.vulkan.desc: Minecraft 1.20.1 has no built-in Vulkan — native Vulkan only arrived in 26.4. For 1.20.1 it comes from the VulkanMod mod (Fabric only): it replaces the whole renderer, so it's enabled by installing the mod, not by a switch. It is incompatible with Sodium, Iris and many rendering mods; Arc HUD effects (shader, render scale, TSR) are disabled under it.
archud.fx.gl_version.desc: Which OpenGL context version to request at launch. Auto — as Minecraft does. 3.2–4.6 — Core profile. 2.0–3.1 — legacy context like Minecraft 1.16, for old GPUs without OpenGL 3.2 (works only if the driver still has the needed features). Versions above your GPU are hidden. Barely affects FPS. Applied after restart; on Forge it edits fml.toml. If the game fails to start with the chosen version, it goes back to Auto next launch.
archud.fx.gl_version.reverted: The game failed to start with the chosen OpenGL version — back to Auto.
archud.fx.gl_current.desc: OpenGL version the driver gave this session.
archud.fx.gl_max.desc: Highest OpenGL version the GPU has reported (in Core profile drivers give the highest supported).
archud.fx.restart.desc: Apply the new OpenGL version: the game closes and reopens (with the open world).

archud.config.antiCrash: Anti-crash (back to menu after a crash)
archud.perf.x_fast_paintings.desc: Paintings are drawn with fewer faces and look the same: pieces with equal light merge, inner edges and the back (when not visible) are skipped. A 4×4 painting: 96 → 17 faces.
archud.perf.p_light_cache.desc: A particle's light is recomputed only when it moves to another block or every 10 ticks, not every frame.
archud.perf.p_async.desc: With more than 400 particles, plain vanilla particles update on several threads. Modded and complex particles (fireworks, drips, lava) stay on the main thread. If a particle type turns out incompatible, it's moved back automatically. Not with OptiFine.
